title: GoA BBG3 lease sale confirms stable leasing cadence
gist: The third Gulf of America Big Beautiful Gulf lease sale on 12 August 2026 drew US$99.5 million across 69 bids for 59 blocks from 16 companies, just short of Wood Mackenzie's US$100-125 million pre-sale expectation, with average high bids down 10% to US$300 per acre. Murphy outspent Chevron at US$21.4 million and took the highest single bid of US$7.7 million for Blacktip, building a material discovered-resource position in Alaminos Canyon, while deepwater took 98% of high-bid value and the shelf just 2%. Wood Mackenzie's stated open question is no longer acreage appetite but when operators convert lease inventory into drilling commitments.

insights.claim: The BBG3 Gulf of America lease sale raised US$99.5 million across 69 bids for 59 blocks, falling just short of Wood Mackenzie's pre-sale expectation of approximately US$100-125 million.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A modest miss against the low end of expectations signals disciplined rather than exuberant acreage bidding in the US offshore.
insights.quote: Total bids reached US$99.5 million across 69 bids for 59 blocks, falling just short of Wood Mackenzie’s pre-sale expectations of approximately US$100–125 million.
insights.locator: The Gulf of America (GoA) Big Beautiful Gulf 3

insights.claim: Sixteen companies participated in BBG3, up from 13 in BBG2, and activity levels landed between BBG2's 25 blocks and BBG1's 181 — the pattern Wood Mackenzie reads as the market finding its rhythm under the new leasing cadence.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Widening participation with mid-range block counts suggests a stable, predictable leasing programme that supports multi-year US offshore capex planning.
insights.quote: Activity levels landed between BBG2's 25 blocks and BBG1's 181, confirming the market is finding its rhythm under the new leasing cadence.
insights.locator: The Gulf of America (GoA) Big Beautiful Gulf 3

insights.claim: The average high bid fell 10% to US$300 per acre from BBG2's US$334 per acre even as participant numbers rose, meaning broader participation came with lower per-acre pricing rather than escalation.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: More bidders paying less per acre implies improved acreage availability rather than intensifying competition — a cost tailwind for Gulf operators.
insights.quote: The average high bid came in at US$300 per acre, down 10% from BBG2's US$334 per acre.

insights.claim: Recently relinquished blocks made up 53% of targeted deepwater blocks, showing that fresh availability of previously held acreage — not new geology — is the primary driver of competition in the basin.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Lease-sale intensity is a function of the relinquishment cycle; forecast future sale demand by tracking expiring leases rather than commodity prices alone.
insights.quote: Recently relinquished blocks made up 53% of targeted deepwater blocks, underscoring that fresh availability continues to drive competition in the basin.

insights.claim: Companies returned to BBG3 with refreshed budgets, more mature seismic data and greater access to newly relinquished acreage, indicating bidding was underpinned by improved subsurface information rather than speculative land-grabbing.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Better-informed bidding raises the probability that this acreage converts to drilling rather than sitting idle.
insights.quote: Companies returned with refreshed budgets, more mature seismic data, and greater access to newly relinquished acreage,

insights.claim: Murphy led all companies in total high-bid spend at US$21.4 million, narrowly outspending Chevron, which won the most blocks — a split between the biggest spender and the biggest acreage winner.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Murphy paying up per block while Chevron spreads across more blocks reveals two opposite Gulf strategies: targeted discovered-resource capture versus optionality.
insights.quote: Murphy led all companies in total high-bid spend at US$21.4 million, narrowly ahead of Chevron, which won the most blocks.
insights.locator: Murphy stakes a bold claim in Alaminos Canyon

insights.claim: Murphy secured the Blacktip block (AC 380) for US$7.7 million, the single highest bid of the sale, alongside Leopard (AC 691).
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The highest single bid of the sale identifies Blacktip as the most contested piece of prospective value — a marker for where the basin's remaining upside is perceived.
insights.quote: Murphy's most significant move was securing the Blacktip block (AC 380) for US$7.7 million, the sale's single highest bid, alongside Leopard (AC 691).
insights.locator: Murphy stakes a bold claim in Alaminos Canyon

insights.claim: Combined with its earlier Baha acquisition from BBG1, Murphy has now assembled a material discovered-resource position across Alaminos Canyon, turning three separate lease sales into a coherent area strategy.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A concentrated discovered-resource block in one canyon is the setup for a hub development decision — watch Murphy for a Alaminos Canyon FID or partner-farm-down.
insights.quote: Together with its earlier Baha acquisition from BBG1, Murphy has built a material discovered-resource position across Alaminos Canyon.
insights.locator: Murphy stakes a bold claim in Alaminos Canyon

insights.claim: The most contested block of the sale was KC 258, attracting four bids totalling US$18.8 million, with BP winning at US$7.5 million ahead of Chevron, Shell and Oxy.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Four Majors bidding on one block flags KC 258 as a consensus high-quality prospect — a signal of where the technical community sees remaining Gulf upside.
insights.quote: The most contested block was KC 258, which attracted four bids totalling US$18.8 million; BP won with a US$7.5 million offer, beating out Chevron, Shell, and Oxy.
insights.locator: Murphy stakes a bold claim in Alaminos Canyon

themes.theme: Deepwater dominance and the drilling conversion question

insights.claim: Deepwater accounted for 80% of all high bids by count and 98% of total high-bid value while the shelf represented just 2% of value, confirming the US Gulf shelf is effectively abandoned as an exploration target.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Any thesis on Gulf shelf revival is unsupported by capital flows; deepwater-capable rig and subsea equipment demand is where the Gulf spend lands.
insights.quote: Deepwater dominated activity, accounting for 80% of all high bids by count and 98% of total high-bid value. Shelf activity remained subdued, representing just 2% of total high-bid value.
insights.locator: The average high bid came in at

insights.claim: Total high bids across shelf and deepwater reached US$82.7 million against US$99.5 million in total bids, meaning roughly 17% of bid dollars went to losing bids — a measure of competitive overlap in the sale.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The gap between total and high bids quantifies genuine head-to-head competition, concentrated on a handful of contested blocks like KC 258.
insights.quote: Total high bids across shelf and deepwater reached US$82.7 million.
insights.locator: The average high bid came in at

insights.claim: With three BBG sales on record, Wood Mackenzie argues the key question has shifted away from acreage appetite entirely to the timing of when operators convert growing lease inventory into actual drilling commitments.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Lease sale results are no longer the informative signal for Gulf activity — rig contracting and exploration well commitments are the metrics that now matter.
insights.quote: The key question is no longer about acreage appetite, it is when operators convert their growing lease inventory into drilling commitments,
insights.locator: With three BBG sales now on record
